clue.text: Make black dynasty appealing

parts.note: to char is to scorch black

explanation.surface: An instruction to paint a ruling dynasty black and make it attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: "Make black" reads like a paint job, but it is the verb for scorching.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe a person or thing that attracts and pleases.

clue.text: Brought up lingerie edged with fleece, a help when dating?

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing a word up reads it bottom to top

parts.note: to fleece someone is to con them

indicators.note: the other word forms a border on both sides, so it goes round the outside

explanation.surface: Frilly underwear trimmed with fleece, offered as a tip for a romantic evening.
explanation.walkthrough: The dating is not romance but scientific dating of old organic remains; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiocarbon dating measures a decaying isotope of this element to age ancient remains, so it is literally a help when dating.

clue.text: Provide weapons for Gulf, where things might be hairy?

explanation.surface: Arming a Gulf state, where the situation might get hairy.
explanation.walkthrough: "Hairy" in the surface means dangerous; in the definition it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a part of the body where hair grows.

clue.text: How one works on fair to get extra income

parts.note: modus operandi, the way one works
fair, as in pale in colour

explanation.surface: Someone working on a fairground stall to earn a bit on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is short for modus operandi, one's method of working.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means taking a second, often secret, job at night for extra money.

clue.text: State board promoting north-east

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoting the letters NE moves them up to the top of the word

parts.note: a board of experts; its last two letters are NE, the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: A state committee promoting the north-east region.
explanation.walkthrough: Only NE moves: lifted from the end of the board word to its front, the rest stays in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a Himalayan country, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Rich vein covering a day

indicators.note: a cover goes over something, so the vein wraps round the A

explanation.surface: A rich seam of ore uncovered in a single day.
explanation.walkthrough: "Covering" takes only the A; the day follows on after.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal slang: someone with plenty of money is rich.

clue.text: Killer vehicle almost missing MOT

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the three letters of MOT are taken out of what remains
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the vehicle word is dropped

explanation.surface: A dangerous car, nearly falling apart, has no MOT certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts MOTORCAR to MOTORCA, and 'missing' takes out MOT. The MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for cars, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is also called the killer whale, so it is known simply as a killer.

clue.text: Private feature of St Paul's brief criticism

parts.note: St Paul's Cathedral in London is famous for its dome
STICK, criticism, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A private detail of St Paul's Cathedral drawing short, sharp criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: To give someone stick is British slang for criticising them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of home and family life, as opposed to public affairs.

clue.text: Put on The Godfather?

definitions.meaning: the title of a Mafia boss such as Vito Corleone

explanation.surface: Screening The Godfather.
explanation.walkthrough: "Put on" suggests staging the film; it means to dress in. The question mark marks the Godfather as one example of a Mafia boss.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to get dressed in a garment; the other is the Italian honorific given to a Mafia head.

clue.text: Any real musical periodically dropped in song of praise

indicators.note: letters dropped at regular periods, so every other one goes

explanation.surface: Any genuine musical number has been cut from a hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd-numbered letters of the two words are the ones thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebrew-derived cry of praise to God, sung in hymns and liturgy.

clue.text: Australian bouncer grabbing setter's lover

indicators.note: to grab is to take hold of, so the outer word closes round the other

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman in Australia getting hold of the puzzle-setter's boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bouncer" is not a doorman but a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym: Shakespeare's young hero gave his name to any ardent male lover.

clue.text: Force member's awkward clam open when touring island

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy, so the letters come out in an ungainly order
a tour goes round a place, so these letters go round the island

explanation.surface: A member of the armed forces awkwardly prising open a clam on an island tour.
explanation.walkthrough: "Force" is the police force, not the military.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a member of the police force.

clue.text: Window that is left on order after vacation

indicators.note: on means placed after in an across answer, so the abbreviation pieces follow
a vacated word is emptied of its inside, so only the first and last letters of order stay

parts.note: first and last letters of order
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An instruction about a window that was left after an order was cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' is the emptying of a word, not a holiday: 'after vacation' keeps just the outer letters of order, and 'on' attaches the two abbreviations after them.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is a bay window projecting from an upper storey of a building.

clue.text: Albanian money includes English national emblem

indicators.note: to include is to hold within

explanation.surface: Albanian currency featuring an English national symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: The emblem wanted is Welsh, not English: "English" only supplies the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this vegetable is the national emblem of Wales.

clue.text: University service ignoring defect in drug addict

explanation.surface: A campus support service that overlooks a flaw in someone on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: A vice is a moral defect, and it sits neatly at the end of the service word.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: someone who takes drugs habitually.

clue.text: Boil second half of drink

indicators.note: taking only the second half of the eight-letter drink word means the first four letters are dropped

explanation.surface: A recipe step: bring the drink to the boil for the second half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second half of' keeps the last four letters of BEVERAGE. 'Boil' looks like a kitchen instruction, but it is the definition in the sense of seethe with anger.
explanation.definitionFit: To boil with anger is to seethe or be furious, the verb sense of rage.

clue.text: Late bloomer caught fruit bobbing across lake

indicators.note: as in catching what someone says: take the sound

parts.note: the ugli fruit, a citrus hybrid

indicators.note: stretched across something, so the word spans either side of it

explanation.surface: Fruit bobbing about on a lake, just as a late-flowering plant is caught up.
explanation.walkthrough: "Caught" looks like cricket's C, but it means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: From Andersen's fairy tale: the scorned cygnet that grows into a swan, so anyone who blossoms late.

clue.text: Unknown author not at first compliant

parts.note: algebra's unknowns are x, y and z
Henry FIELDING, author of Tom Jones, without his F

explanation.surface: An anonymous writer who wasn't cooperative at first.
explanation.walkthrough: "Not at first" reads as a timeline, but it strips the author's initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: giving way readily to pressure or requests.

clue.text: Begin kid's first tracksuit, wrongly having lost uniform

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of kid
wrongly says the remaining letters are put in the wrong order
having lost means one letter is gone from the tracksuit before the jumble

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A child starts out in a tracksuit, worn the wrong way, having lost the school uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost uniform' takes the U out of tracksuit to leave TRACKSIT, and 'wrongly' rearranges that into ICKSTART after the K of kid.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick-start something is to get it going with a sudden push, as a motorbike is started with a kick.

clue.text: Revered figure's form of cricket before noon

parts.note: One Day International, a cricket format

explanation.surface: A cricketing hero's style of play before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-day international is a limited-overs cricket match between national teams.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the chief god of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Tunbridge Wells weirdly not having gel, but somehow he profits dishonestly

indicators.note: weirdly suggests the letters of the town are jumbled
not having means the named letters are taken out of the pool
somehow confirms the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be removed
taken as written, letters to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone in the Kent spa town of Tunbridge Wells is a crook making money without hair gel.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters G, E, L, B, U, T out of TUNBRIDGE WELLS; the remaining eight letters rearrange into the answer. Tunbridge Wells is a genteel town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler is a cheat who obtains money by fraud, gaining from deceit.

clue.text: Miserable work on the house, eating what toast?

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside, so the outer word swallows the other

parts.note: to put a straw roof on a house

explanation.surface: Grim renovation work, then eating toast.
explanation.walkthrough: "Toast" suggests bread, but it is a drinking toast; the two-letter query goes in after the roofing word's second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: said as a toast before knocking back a drink.

clue.text: Pupil picked up skirt

indicators.note: as a radio picks up a signal: what is heard

parts.note: a pupil living at boarding school

explanation.surface: A schoolchild grabbing a skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: "Skirt" looks like a garment, but it is the verb: to skirt a field is to run along its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to skirt something is to lie along its edge.

clue.text: Medical centre welcomes queen, not popular minister

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the queen's letters go inside what is left of the clinic
not popular means the letters for popular are removed

parts.note: a clinic is a medical centre
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher of the Queen

explanation.surface: A health centre greets the queen, though the minister there is not well liked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not popular' takes IN out of CLINIC to leave CLIC, and 'welcomes' brings ER into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a member of the clergy, and minister is another name for such a church official.

clue.text: About to abandon dog in square

indicators.note: what abandons a word leaves it, so those letters go

parts.note: a member of the dog family

explanation.surface: Being told to abandon your dog in the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: "Square" means a square number, not a town square.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: three squared, a square number.

clue.text: Unintroduced woman who raised Cain?

indicators.note: unintroduced means lacking an introduction, so the opening letter of the woman word goes

parts.note: madam is a polite form of address for a woman

explanation.surface: A mysterious woman, never introduced, who caused a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unintroduced' drops the opening M of MADAM. To raise Cain is to cause trouble, which fits the surface; literally, Adam was Cain's father in Genesis, so he raised Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man is the father of Cain, so he literally brought up that son.

clue.text: Prophet Hosea extremely bereft in written document

indicators.note: in places the trimmed name inside the abbreviation for a document

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a written document

indicators.note: bereft of its extremes means the first and last letters of Hosea are lost

parts.note: Hosea without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The prophet Hosea is utterly grief-stricken in a written text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hosea' is itself a prophet, tempting you to take it as the definition; 'extremely bereft' strips its ends, and 'in' sets what is left inside the manuscript abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses is regarded as a prophet in Judaism, Christianity and Islam, leader of the Israelites.

clue.text: Damage earth around edge of park

indicators.note: around means the earth word goes round the letter from park
the edge of park here is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Digging up the soil around the edge of a park damages it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edge of' gives the P of park, which SOIL wraps around.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil something is to ruin or impair it, the same as damaging it.

clue.text: Grind cold cut

parts.note: to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Grinding up a cold cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cold cut" reads as sliced meat, but the phrase splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: working food between the teeth.

clue.text: Hard veterans show affection

explanation.surface: Tough old soldiers showing a soft side.
explanation.walkthrough: "Hard veterans" looks like one tough group, but hard supplies only its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: clasping another's hand is a gesture of affection.

clue.text: Carrion eaters no longer having desire for bears

indicators.note: the scavengers no longer have those letters, so they come out

explanation.surface: Scavengers that have lost their appetite for bears.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bears" looks like the animals, but it is the verb, as in bearing a scar.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to bear something is to carry or possess it.

clue.text: Maybe how to form a comparative adjective for snake

definitions.text: how to form a comparative adjective
definitions.meaning: the instruction for turning big into bigger, read as two words

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on the right comparative for a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, the answer splits into a verb and a suffix: fast becomes faster. "Maybe" admits not every comparative works this way.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the viper, Britain's only venomous snake; the other is the instruction to tack a suffix onto an adjective.

clue.text: Stretch limo initially bends round

indicators.note: turned round, so the letters are read back to front
at its start, so only the word's opening letter

explanation.surface: A stretch limousine negotiating the bends.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stretch limo" is a single phrase in the surface; split it, and the first word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to spread or extend out loosely.

clue.text: Strangely secret, with each bit hidden?

indicators.note: arranged strangely, so the letters are in an odd order

parts.note: a binary bit is 0 or 1, read as the letters O and I

explanation.surface: A strangely secret code with every bit concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bit" is the computing term: each bit is a 0 or a 1, which pass as O and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: knowledge understood only by an inner circle is in effect hidden.
